Check the Exact Date, Trayodashi Tithi and Puja Muhurat 
 Neeraj Dhankher / TOI Astrology / Nov 03, 2026, 12:30 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print In 2026, Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6, as per the lunar calendar. This auspicious day aligns with Dhanvantari Jayanti and Shukra Pradosh Vrat. It is advisable to make purchases after 10:30 AM. The evening puja is best performed during Pradosh kaal, which is from 6:02 PM to 7:57 PM. The celebrations will continue until Bhai Dooj on November 10, enhancing the festive spirit of Diwali week. When is Dhanteras this year? If you’ve seen 5 November floating around, it’s easy to see where the mix-up comes from. Hindu festivals follow the tithi, the lunar day, and the tithi rarely lines up neatly with the calendar date. Dhanteras belongs to Trayodashi, the thirteenth day of the waning Moon in Kartik. In 2026, that tithi only begins on Friday morning. Thursday the 5th has its own festivals anyway. It’s Rama Ekadashi, and in the evening, Govatsa Dwadashi. So Why Friday and Not Thursday? 
 Dwadashi starts at around 10:35 AM (Delhi, IST) on Thursday and carries on until about 10:30 AM on Friday. Trayodashi takes over from there and runs till roughly 10:47 AM on Saturday, 7 November. The deciding factor is the evening. Lakshmi-Kubera puja on Dhanteras has to happen in pradosh kaal, the stretch of time just after sunset, while Trayodashi is still running. Friday evening ticks that box completely. Saturday doesn’t, because by sunset the tithi has already shifted to Chaturdashi. That leaves Friday, 6 November, as the only correct date, and it’s what every standard Panchang shows. When Can You Buy? 
 Anything bought after about 10:30 AM on Friday counts as a Dhanteras purchase, whether it’s a coin, a utensil or a piece of jewellery. Still, a lot of families like to finish their shopping by late afternoon. That way the new item can sit in front of Lakshmi and Kubera during the evening puja, which feels like the proper way to bring it home. The Best Time for Puja 
 The ideal window is when pradosh kaal overlaps with Vrishabha lagna. Vrishabha is a fixed sign, and the old belief is that wealth welcomed under a fixed lagna stays put. In New Delhi, pradosh kaal stretches from roughly 5:33 PM to 8:09 PM. Inside that, the best puja time is 6:02 PM to 7:57 PM. Gurugram is almost identical, at 6:03 PM to 7:59 PM. Jaipur’s window opens a little later, from 6:11 PM to 8:07 PM. Down south, Chennai has 6:14 PM to 8:10 PM and Hyderabad 6:15 PM to 8:13 PM. Pune sits furthest west of these, so its puja time runs from 6:32 PM to 8:31 PM. For anywhere else, go by local sunset. The window moves a few minutes either way. More Than One Festival That Evening 
 Friday isn’t only about wealth. It’s also Dhanvantari Jayanti, marking the birth of the divine healer linked with Ayurveda, so a prayer for good health fits in naturally beside the prayer for prosperity. Being a Friday Trayodashi, it’s Shukra Pradosh Vrat as well, and many people offer prayers to Lord Shiva at twilight. After the main puja, don’t forget the Yama Deep. It’s a single lamp with four wicks, placed outside the front door and facing south. Families light it as a quiet prayer that no one in the house is lost before their time. Go Easy on the Big Purchases 
 There’s one astrological wrinkle this year. On Dhanteras morning, retrograde Venus slips into Virgo, the sign where it’s weakest. Venus rules gold, silver and luxuries in general, so 2026 favours sensible, smaller buys over expensive ones. A silver coin or a brass diya does the job perfectly well. So does a new steel pot for the kitchen. The Rest of Diwali Week 
 Choti Diwali, or Naraka Chaturdashi, comes on Saturday, 7 November. The main Diwali and Lakshmi Puja fall on Sunday, 8 November. Govardhan Puja follows on Monday, and Bhai Dooj closes the festival on Tuesday, 10 November.
